question: ________ was posthumously conferred the second-highest civilian award in India, the Padma Vibhushan in the field of public affairs in 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mulayam Singh Yadav.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mulayam Singh Yadav, founder of the Samajwadi Party and former Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh and Union Defence Minister, was posthumously conferred the Padma Vibhushan — India's second-highest civilian award — in the field of Public Affairs at the 2023 Republic Day honours. (मुलायम सिंह यादव — पद्म विभूषण, लोक सेवा)

 

• He passed away on 10 October 2022; the award recognised his long career in public life and Indian politics.

 

• The Padma Vibhushan is awarded for "exceptional and distinguished service" and ranks immediately below the Bharat Ratna in India's civilian honours system.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Awards (Vibhushan, Bhushan, Shri) are announced annually on the eve of Republic Day by the President of India on the recommendation of the Padma Awards Committee.

 

• The 2023 list also included Zakir Hussain and S.M. Krishna among the Padma Vibhushan awardees.

 

NOTE

 

• GMC Balayogi (Option 1): A former Speaker of the Lok Sabha who died in a helicopter crash in 2002; not a 2023 Padma Vibhushan recipient.

 

• Dilip Mahalanabis (Option 2): Pioneer of Oral Rehydration Therapy (ORS), also posthumously awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 2023, but in the field of Medicine, not Public Affairs.

 

• Balkrishna Doshi (Option 4): Renowned architect and Pritzker Prize laureate, also posthumously awarded the Padma Vibhushan in 2023, but in the field of Literature & Education, not Public Affairs.

question: A proton bonds to the oxygen atom of a solvent water to give a _______________________ hydronium ion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is trigonal pyramidal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a proton (H⁺) bonds to the oxygen atom of a water molecule, it forms the hydronium ion (H₃O⁺). (हाइड्रोनियम आयन — त्रिकोणीय पिरामिडाकार)

 

• The oxygen atom in H₃O⁺ is sp³ hybridised, with three bond pairs (to the three hydrogen atoms) and one lone pair of electrons.

 

• Because one of the four electron domains is a lone pair, the molecular geometry (shape) is trigonal pyramidal — the same basic shape as ammonia (NH₃), which is also isoelectronic with H₃O⁺.

 

• The electron-pair geometry around oxygen is tetrahedral, but the molecular shape (which describes only the arrangement of atoms) is trigonal pyramidal because the lone pair, though occupying space, is not counted as a “bonded” position.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The H-O-H bond angle in hydronium is about 113°, slightly larger than in water (104.5°) due to increased bond-pair repulsion.

 

• Hydronium ion formation explains why pure water shows weak self-ionisation: 2H₂O ⇌ H₃O⁺ + OH⁻.

 

NOTE

 

• Square pyramid (Option 1): This shape requires five bonded/lone electron domains (e.g., in BrF₅), not applicable to a 4-domain oxygen centre.

 

• Tetrahedral (Option 3): This describes the electron-pair geometry, not the actual molecular shape, since one domain is a lone pair rather than a bonded atom.

 

• Square planar (Option 4): This shape arises from six electron domains with two lone pairs (e.g., XeF₄), not relevant to H₃O⁺.

question: In July 2021, which state government announced the creation of an independent department to protect and preserve the ‘faith, culture and traditions of tribes and indigenous communities’ of the state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In July 2021, shortly after Himanta Biswa Sarma took over as Chief Minister, the Assam government approved the creation of a separate Department of Indigenous Faith and Culture to protect and preserve the faith, culture and traditions of the tribal and indigenous communities of the state. (असम — स्वदेशी आस्था और संस्कृति विभाग)

 

• The department was carved out specifically to safeguard tribal belief systems, rituals and cultural practices that were earlier clubbed with other general administrative departments.

 

• This move was part of a broader set of decisions by the new Assam cabinet aimed at tribal welfare and cultural preservation in the state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Assam is home to numerous indigenous and tribal communities such as the Bodo, Mising, Karbi, Tiwa, Rabha and Deori, among others.

 

• Himanta Biswa Sarma became the Chief Minister of Assam in May 2021.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 1): No such dedicated department for indigenous faith and culture was created by the UP government in July 2021.

 

• Bihar (Option 2): No such announcement was made by the Bihar government at this time.

 

• Karnataka (Option 3): No such department was created by the Karnataka government in July 2021.

question: Who among the following is a Choreographer in Indian film Industry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prabhu Deva.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prabhu Deva is a celebrated Indian dancer, choreographer, actor and film director, known for his energetic dance style and choreography in numerous Bollywood and South Indian films. (प्रभु देवा — नृत्य निर्देशक)

 

• He rose to fame with his choreography and performance in songs like "Muqabla" and has since choreographed and directed multiple commercially successful films.

 

• He has won several awards for choreography and is regarded as one of India's most influential dance choreographers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Prabhu Deva has directed films such as "Wanted" and "Rowdy Rathore" and has also acted in films across Tamil, Telugu and Hindi cinema.

 

NOTE

 

• Anu Malik (Option 1): A well-known music director/composer in Bollywood, not a choreographer.

 

• Pritam (Option 2): A prominent Bollywood music director/composer, not a choreographer.

 

• Arijit Singh (Option 4): A leading Indian playback singer, not a choreographer.

question: Which does social networking service place the biggest emphasis on professional networking?
solution_text:
The correct answer is LinkedIn.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• LinkedIn is a social networking platform specifically designed for professional networking, career development, job searching and business connections. (लिंक्डइन — व्यावसायिक नेटवर्किंग)

 

• Launched in 2003, it allows users to build professional profiles, connect with colleagues and recruiters, and showcase work experience, skills and endorsements.

 

• It is widely used by businesses and professionals for recruitment, B2B networking and career growth, distinguishing it from platforms built primarily for personal/social interaction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• LinkedIn is currently owned by Microsoft, which acquired it in 2016.

 

NOTE

 

• Facebook (Option 1): Primarily a personal/social networking platform for friends and family.

 

• Google+ (Option 2): Google's now-discontinued general-purpose social networking service.

 

• Twitter (Option 4): A microblogging and social media platform focused on short public posts, not primarily professional networking.

question: ‘Lai-Phi’ and ‘Chin-Phi’ are the cultural costumes of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• ‘Lai-Phi’ and ‘Chin-Phi’ are traditional wrap-around garments worn by the Meitei community of Manipur, forming part of the state's distinctive costume tradition. (लाई-फी, चिन-फी — मणिपुर)

 

• In Manipuri (Meitei), the term ‘Phi’ refers to cloth/wrap, and different types of Phi (such as Phanek, Innaphi, Lai Phi and Chin Phi) are worn on different occasions, including rituals and festivals.

 

• Manipur's traditional attire also includes the Phanek (a wrap-around skirt worn by women) and the Innaphi (a wrap/stole).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Manipur is also known for classical Manipuri dance, one of the eight classical dance forms of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Nagaland (Option 1): Known for tribal shawls and costumes distinct to its various Naga tribes, not for Lai-Phi/Chin-Phi.

 

• Uttarakhand (Option 2): Known for costumes like the Ghagra-Choli and Pichaura, not Lai-Phi/Chin-Phi.

 

• Sikkim (Option 4): Known for costumes like the Bakhu, not Lai-Phi/Chin-Phi.

question: In MS Word, which option allows you to copy the selected text or object to the Clipboard while simultaneously removing it from its original location?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cut.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Cut command (Ctrl+X) removes the selected text or object from its original location and places it on the Clipboard, from where it can be inserted elsewhere using Paste. (कट कमांड — क्लिपबोर्ड में स्थानांतरण)

 

• This is different from Copy, which duplicates the selection onto the Clipboard without removing it from its original location.

 

• The Cut, Copy and Paste commands together form the basic clipboard operations available in MS Word and most other applications.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common MS Word keyboard shortcuts: Ctrl+X (Cut), Ctrl+C (Copy), Ctrl+V (Paste).

 

NOTE

 

• Drag-and-Drop (Option 1): Moves content by dragging it with the mouse; it does not use the Clipboard.

 

• Paste (Option 2): Inserts the content already on the Clipboard into a new location; it does not remove anything from an original location.

 

• Copy (Option 3): Duplicates the selected content onto the Clipboard without deleting it from its original location.

question: The headquarters of the Indian Institute of Tourism and Travel Management are located at:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gwalior.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Institute of Tourism and Travel Management (IITTM) has its headquarters at Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. (भारतीय पर्यटन और यात्रा प्रबंधन संस्थान — ग्वालियर)

 

• IITTM is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, established to promote quality education, training and research in tourism and travel management.

 

• It also has several regional centres across India, including in Delhi, Bhubaneswar, Noida and Gwahati, but its headquarters remains at Gwalior.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• IITTM was established in 1983 and offers programmes such as MBA in Tourism and Travel Management.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhuvneshwar (Option 1): Home to one of IITTM's regional campuses, not its headquarters.

 

• New Delhi (Option 2): Home to another IITTM regional centre (Noida/NCR), not its headquarters.

 

• Guwahati (Option 3): Home to another IITTM regional centre, not its headquarters.

question: In April 2022, Chief Justice of India NV Ramana recommended the creation of an “independent umbrella institution”, so as to bring various agencies under one roof”. Which of the following agencies did he suggest be brought under this umbrella?
solution_text:
The correct answer is ED, CBI and SFIO.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In April 2022, then Chief Justice of India N.V. Ramana recommended creating an independent, autonomous "umbrella institution" to bring central investigating agencies — the Enforcement Directorate (ED), Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) — under one roof. (सीजेआई एनवी रमना — छत्र संस्था प्रस्ताव)

 

• He made this suggestion while speaking about the need for structural, financial and functional autonomy for investigating agencies to insulate them from political and executive influence.

 

• The remarks were made in the context of concerns over the independence of premier investigation agencies in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• N.V. Ramana served as the 48th Chief Justice of India, from April 2021 to August 2022.

 

• The CBI functions under the Department of Personnel and Training, the ED under the Ministry of Finance, and the SFIO under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

 

NOTE

 

• SFIO and CBI (Option 2): Incomplete — omits the ED, which CJI Ramana explicitly included.

 

• ED and NIA (Option 3): Incorrect combination — the NIA was not part of this specific proposal; SFIO was, not the NIA.

 

• CBI, SFIO and NIA (Option 4): Incorrect — substitutes the NIA for the ED, which was not part of the recommendation.

question: Gurpurab is celebrated to commemorate the birthday of Guru Nank dev ji. He was the _________ guru of Sikhs?
solution_text:
The correct answer is first.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Nanak Dev Ji was the first of the ten Sikh Gurus and the founder of Sikhism. (गुरु नानक देव जी — प्रथम सिख गुरु)

 

• His birthday is celebrated as Guru Nanak Gurpurab (or Guru Nanak Jayanti), typically falling on the full moon (Kartik Purnima) in the month of Kartik.

 

• He propagated the core Sikh principles of one God (Ik Onkar), honest living, and equality among all human beings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The tenth and last Sikh Guru was Guru Gobind Singh Ji, who founded the Khalsa Panth in 1699.

 

• After Guru Gobind Singh, the Guru Granth Sahib was declared the eternal, living Guru of the Sikhs.

 

NOTE

 

• Second (Option 1): Refers to Guru Angad Dev Ji, the second Sikh Guru, not Guru Nanak.

 

• Third (Option 2): Refers to Guru Amar Das Ji, the third Sikh Guru.

 

• Fourth (Option 4): Refers to Guru Ram Das Ji, the fourth Sikh Guru, founder of Amritsar.

question: In which direction is the general elevation of the peninsular plateau of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is From West to East.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Peninsular Plateau of India has a general elevation that slopes from west to east, which is why most of the major peninsular rivers (Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Mahanadi) flow eastward and drain into the Bay of Bengal. (प्रायद्वीपीय पठार — पश्चिम से पूर्व ढाल)

 

• The plateau is bounded by the Western Ghats (higher, closer to the Arabian Sea) and the Eastern Ghats (lower, more discontinuous), reinforcing this west-to-east tilt.

 

• Exceptions such as the Narmada and Tapi rivers flow westward through rift valleys, but the general elevation trend of the plateau itself is west to east.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Peninsular Plateau is one of the oldest and most stable landmasses in India, formed from Gondwana land.

 

• It is divided into the Central Highlands (north of the Narmada) and the Deccan Plateau (south of the Narmada).

 

NOTE

 

• North to South, South to North, East to West (Options 1, 3, 4): These do not represent the actual west-to-east tilt of the Peninsular Plateau, which is established by the eastward flow of its major rivers.

question:
All historical monuments have signages with instructions that public should not write on the walls.

To which fundamental duty does the given statement belong?
option_2: To defend the country and render national service
option_3: To promote harmony and spirit of common brotherhood
option_4: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
solution_text:
The correct answer is To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 51A(i) of the Indian Constitution, it is a Fundamental Duty of every citizen "to safeguard public property and to abjure violence". (सार्वजनिक संपत्ति की रक्षा — मौलिक कर्तव्य)

 

• Historical monuments are examples of public property, and instructing people not to deface or write on their walls is a direct application of this duty.

 

• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties listed under Article 51A, found in Part IVA of the Constitution.

 

• The 11th duty (to provide opportunities for education to children between 6-14 years) was added later by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

NOTE

 

• To develop the scientific temper (Option 1): Article 51A(h) — relates to developing scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry, not property protection.

 

• To defend the country and render national service (Option 2): Article 51A(d) — relates to national defence and service, not monument protection.

 

• To promote harmony and spirit of common brotherhood (Option 3): Article 51A(e) — relates to communal harmony among all citizens, not public property protection.

question: Where is the largest football stadium in India located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kolkata.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan (Salt Lake Stadium) in Kolkata, West Bengal, is the largest football stadium in India and one of the largest stadiums in the world by seating capacity. (साल्ट लेक स्टेडियम, कोलकाता — सबसे बड़ा फुटबॉल स्टेडियम)

 

• It was originally built with a capacity exceeding 1,20,000, later renovated and reduced to around 85,000, and hosts major football matches, including ISL and international fixtures.

 

• It is a multi-purpose stadium that also hosts athletics events, but is best known as India's premier football venue.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kolkata is often called the "Mecca of Indian Football" due to its strong football culture and historic clubs like Mohun Bagan and East Bengal.

 

NOTE

 

• Goa (Option 2): Home to the Fatorda Stadium, a significant but smaller football venue.

 

• Bengaluru (Option 3): Home to the Sree Kanteerava Stadium, smaller in capacity than Salt Lake Stadium.

 

• New Delhi (Option 4): Home to the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium, a multi-purpose stadium but not the largest football venue in India.

question: In which of the following years was the National Anthem adopted in its Hindi version by the Constituent Assembly?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1950.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constituent Assembly of India adopted the Hindi version of "Jana Gana Mana" as the National Anthem of India on 24 January 1950, a day before the country formally became a republic. (राष्ट्रगान — जन गण मन, 24 जनवरी 1950)

 

• The song was originally composed in Bengali by Rabindranath Tagore and was first sung in 1911 at the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress.

 

• The National Anthem takes about 52 seconds to sing in its full version, and a shortened version (first and last lines) takes about 20 seconds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's National Song, "Vande Mataram", was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and given equal status with the National Anthem by the Constituent Assembly.

 

NOTE

 

• 1947 (Option 1): The year of India's independence, not the adoption of the National Anthem.

 

• 1942 (Option 3): Not associated with the adoption of the National Anthem; this year is associated with the Quit India Movement.

 

• 1954 (Option 4): Not the year of adoption of the National Anthem.

question: _________ oblong orbit overlaps the orbit of Neptune.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pluto's.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pluto's highly elongated (oblong/elliptical) orbit around the Sun is so eccentric that it periodically crosses inside the orbit of Neptune. (प्लूटो की कक्षा — नेपच्यून की कक्षा को पार करना)

 

• From 1979 to 1999, Pluto was actually closer to the Sun than Neptune, due to this orbital overlap.

 

• Because of its small size, eccentric orbit and orbital overlap with Neptune, Pluto was reclassified as a "dwarf planet" by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in 2006.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pluto's orbit is also inclined at about 17 degrees to the ecliptic plane, unlike the more aligned orbits of the eight major planets.

 

• Pluto is part of the Kuiper Belt, a region of icy bodies beyond Neptune's orbit.

 

NOTE

 

• Mars' (Option 1): Mars has a moderately elliptical orbit but does not overlap Neptune's orbit.

 

• Jupiter's (Option 3): Jupiter's orbit lies well within Neptune's and does not overlap it.

 

• Venus' (Option 4): Venus has a nearly circular orbit close to the Sun, nowhere near Neptune's orbit.

question:
Match the columns.

List I

i. National Manufacturing Policy

ii. Make in India initiative

iii. Startup India scheme

iv. Smart City Project

List II

a. 2014

b. 2016

c. 2011

d. 2015
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-c, ii-a, iii-b, iv-d.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The National Manufacturing Policy was announced in 2011 (i-c), aiming to raise the share of manufacturing in GDP to 25% and create jobs. (राष्ट्रीय विनिर्माण नीति — 2011)

 

• The Make in India initiative was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 25 September 2014 (ii-a) to boost domestic manufacturing and attract foreign investment.

 

• The Startup India scheme was launched on 16 January 2016 (iii-b) to build a strong ecosystem for nurturing innovation and startups.

 

• The Smart City Mission was launched on 25 June 2015 (iv-d), aiming to develop 100 smart cities across India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Make in India uses a lion as its logo, symbolising manufacturing strength and national growth.

 

• The Smart City Mission and AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation) were launched together in 2015.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (i-d, ii-c, iii-a, iv-b): Incorrectly assigns 2015 to the Manufacturing Policy and 2011 to Make in India, reversing the actual years.

 

• Option 2 (i-b, ii-a, iii-d, iv-c): Incorrectly assigns 2016 to the Manufacturing Policy and 2015 to Startup India.

 

• Option 4 (i-c, ii-d, iii-b, iv-a): Incorrectly assigns 2015 to Make in India and 2014 to the Smart City Project, reversing their actual years.

question: Lakshmibai National College of Physical Education is located at ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lakshmibai National College of Physical Education (LNCPE) is located at Kariavattom, Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala. (लक्ष्मीबाई राष्ट्रीय शारीरिक शिक्षा महाविद्यालय — तिरुवनंतपुरम)

 

• It functions as a constituent unit affiliated to the Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education (LNIPE), which is a deemed university and is itself headquartered in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh.

 

• LNCPE offers undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in physical education and sports sciences.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The LNIPE (Lakshmibai National Institute of Physical Education) at Gwalior was established in 1957 and is often confused with LNCPE due to their similar names.

 

NOTE

 

• Shahdara, Delhi (Option 1): Not the location of LNCPE.

 

• Patiala, Punjab (Option 2): Home to the National Institute of Sports (NIS), a different institution, not LNCPE.

 

• Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): This is the location of the parent institute, LNIPE (deemed university), a commonly confused distractor — but the LNCPE college itself is at Thiruvananthapuram.

question: What is the literacy rate of India as per the National Survey of India-2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 77.7%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the national survey report referenced for 2022 (based on the National Statistical Office's survey data), the literacy rate of India stood at 77.7%. (भारत की साक्षरता दर — 77.7%)

 

• This figure reflects the estimated literacy rate for persons aged 7 years and above, computed from large-scale household survey data conducted by the National Statistical Office (NSO).

 

• This is distinct from the 2011 Census literacy rate, which was recorded at 74.04%, showing an improvement in the years since.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per Census 2011, male literacy stood at about 82.14% and female literacy at about 65.46%, giving an overall rate of ~74%.

 

• Kerala consistently records the highest literacy rate among Indian states.

 

NOTE

 

• 78.3%, 74.2%, 72.1% (Options 1, 2, 3): These do not match the literacy figure reported in the 2022 national survey data referenced by this question.

question: Which of the following word sequences is correct as per the Preamble to the Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic, republic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Preamble to the Indian Constitution describes India as a "SOVEREIGN, SOCIALIST, SECULAR, DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC", in that exact sequence. (प्रस्तावना — संप्रभु, समाजवादी, धर्मनिरपेक्ष, लोकतांत्रिक गणराज्य)

 

• The words "Socialist" and "Secular" were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976; the original 1950 Preamble read only "Sovereign Democratic Republic".

 

• This sequence is a frequently tested detail, as the correct order — Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic — must be remembered precisely.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Preamble also declares India's objectives to secure Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity for all citizens.

 

• The Preamble was famously described by N.A. Palkhivala as the "identity card of the Constitution".

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4: Each rearranges or repeats the words incorrectly, deviating from the Preamble's exact, constitutionally fixed sequence.

question: Which non-essential amino acid is synthesised by the hydroxylation of phenylalanine in a reaction catalysed by phenylalanine hydroxylase?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tyrosine.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tyrosine is a non-essential amino acid synthesised in the body through the hydroxylation of phenylalanine, a reaction catalysed by the enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase. (टायरोसिन — फेनिलएलनिन हाइड्रॉक्सिलेशन)

 

• Since the body can make tyrosine from phenylalanine (an essential amino acid obtained from the diet), tyrosine itself is classified as non-essential, provided sufficient phenylalanine is available.

 

• A deficiency or malfunction of phenylalanine hydroxylase causes the genetic disorder Phenylketonuria (PKU), in which phenylalanine accumulates to toxic levels in the body.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tyrosine is a precursor for important biomolecules such as dopamine, adrenaline, noradrenaline, and thyroid hormones (T3, T4).

 

NOTE

 

• Glutamine (Option 1): A non-essential amino acid, but it is synthesised from glutamate, not from phenylalanine hydroxylation.

 

• Cysteine (Option 3): A non-essential amino acid synthesised from methionine and serine, not from phenylalanine.

 

• Glycine (Option 4): A non-essential amino acid synthesised mainly from serine, not from phenylalanine.

question: Who invaded India during the rule of Tughlaq Dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Timur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Timur (Tamerlane), the Turco-Mongol conqueror, invaded India in 1398 CE, during the reign of Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah Tughlaq, the last ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty. (तैमूर का आक्रमण — तुगलक वंश, 1398)

 

• Timur's invasion led to the sack of Delhi, causing massive destruction and loss of life, and severely weakened the already declining Tughlaq dynasty.

 

• This invasion is considered one of the key events that accelerated the disintegration of the Delhi Sultanate under the Tughlaqs, paving the way for the eventual rise of the Sayyid dynasty.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Tughlaq dynasty ruled from 1320 to 1413 CE, and its notable rulers included Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq, Muhammad bin Tughlaq, and Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

 

NOTE

 

• Mahmud of Ghazni (Option 2): Invaded India between 997-1030 CE, long before the Tughlaq dynasty (which began in 1320) was established.

 

• Chengiz Khan (Option 3): Pursued Jalaluddin Mangburni to the Indus River around 1221 CE, during the reign of Iltutmish of the Slave/Mamluk dynasty, not the Tughlaqs.

 

• Muhammad Ghori (Option 4): Invaded India in the late 12th century (1175-1206 CE), prior to the establishment of the Delhi Sultanate itself, well before the Tughlaq dynasty.

question: What is the impact of proportional taxes?
option_1: Increases the marginal propensity to consume
solution_text:
The correct answer is Reduces the autonomous expenditure multiplier.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A proportional tax takes away a fixed proportion of every additional unit of income earned, acting as a leakage from the income-expenditure circular flow. (आनुपातिक कर — व्यय गुणक में कमी)

 

• Because part of each extra rupee of income is taxed away before it can be spent, proportional taxes reduce the marginal propensity to consume out of gross income, which in turn reduces the size of the autonomous expenditure (income) multiplier.

 

• Mathematically, with a proportional tax rate t, the multiplier becomes 1 / [1 - MPC(1-t)], which is smaller than the no-tax multiplier 1 / (1-MPC).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A smaller multiplier means that changes in autonomous spending (investment, government spending) have a dampened effect on overall national income when proportional taxes exist.

 

• Progressive and proportional taxes both act as automatic stabilisers, reducing the amplitude of business cycle fluctuations.

 

NOTE

 

• Increases the marginal propensity to consume (Option 1): Incorrect — proportional taxes reduce, not increase, the effective MPC out of gross income.

 

• Increases the induced expenditure multiplier (Option 3): Incorrect — a tax leakage reduces, rather than increases, expenditure multipliers.

 

• Increases the autonomous expenditure multiplier (Option 4): Incorrect — this is the opposite of the actual effect of a proportional tax leakage.

question: Annamacharya composed Sankirtans in praise of which God?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Venkateshwara.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Annamacharya (also known as Annamayya), a 15th-century Telugu saint-composer, composed thousands of devotional Sankirtans (Sankeertanas) in praise of Lord Venkateshwara of Tirumala. (अन्नामाचार्य — भगवान वेंकटेश्वर संकीर्तन)

 

• He is regarded as the "Pada Kavita Pitamaha" (grandfather of Telugu devotional song-poetry) and composed over 32,000 Sankirtans, many of which are preserved as copper plate inscriptions at Tirumala.

 

• His compositions are considered pioneering works of Carnatic music and Telugu devotional literature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Annamacharya lived from 1408 to 1503 CE and is closely associated with the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD).

 

• The Andhra Pradesh government has instituted several honours and scholarships in his name for the promotion of Carnatic music.

 

NOTE

 

• Lord Rama (Option 1): Not the deity primarily associated with Annamacharya's Sankirtans.

 

• Lord Krishna (Option 2): Krishna bhakti compositions are more associated with figures like Surdas and Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, not primarily Annamacharya.

 

• Lord Shiva (Option 4): Not the deity Annamacharya's Sankirtans were primarily dedicated to.

question: Which important event that started in 1930 played a significant role in motivating and mobilizing Indians to join the non-violent movement for independence?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Salt Satyagraha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Salt Satyagraha (Dandi March), led by Mahatma Gandhi, began on 12 March 1930 and culminated with Gandhi breaking the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930. (नमक सत्याग्रह — दांडी मार्च, 1930)

 

• It marked the formal start of the Civil Disobedience Movement, mobilising large numbers of ordinary Indians — across class, caste and gender — to defy British colonial law non-violently.

 

• The movement's success in galvanising mass participation made it one of the most significant events in India's independence struggle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Salt Satyagraha directly challenged the British monopoly on salt production and the Salt Tax.

 

• It drew international attention to India's freedom struggle and Gandhi's philosophy of Satyagraha (non-violent resistance).

 

NOTE

 

• Swadeshi movement (Option 1): Began in 1905, in response to the Partition of Bengal, not 1930.

 

• Gadar Movement (Option 2): Founded in 1913 by Indian expatriates in North America, not 1930.

 

• Quit India Movement (Option 3): Began in August 1942, not 1930.

question: What are the standard measurements of a cricket pitch?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 22 yards by 10 ft.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A standard cricket pitch measures 22 yards (66 feet) in length and 10 feet in width, as defined by the Laws of Cricket. (क्रिकेट पिच — 22 गज x 10 फीट)

 

• The 22-yard length is also known as a "chain", a traditional unit of measurement, and represents the distance between the two sets of stumps (bowling and batting ends).

 

• The pitch is a rectangular strip in the centre of the cricket ground on which the bowler bowls and the batter plays their shots.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Each set of stumps is 9 inches wide, and the popping crease is drawn 4 feet in front of the stumps at each end.

 

• The pitch dimensions are standard across all forms of the game — Test, ODI, and T20 cricket.

 

NOTE

 

• 20 yards by 12 ft, 22 yards by 12 ft, 20 yards by 10 ft (Options 1, 2, 3): Each states an incorrect length and/or width; the correct, official dimensions are 22 yards by 10 feet.
